prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Atlanta. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Atlanta for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need one quick detail so I give accurate, local names: what part of Atlanta are you closest to (zip code or neighborhood)? Also tell me whether this is a single-tooth implant, multiple implants or full-arch (All‑on‑4 type), and whether insurance/price or sedation are important to you.

While you reply, here’s useful guidance so you know what I’ll look for and why:

Which types of practices you should call (and why)
- Emory University Dental/Oral Surgery (academic center): great if you want experienced specialists, complex-case expertise, and multidisciplinary care. Good for complicated medical histories.
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons: they place implants surgically and manage extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, IV sedation; call them if you want the surgeon to do the implant placement.
- Board-certified periodontists (implant specialists): focused on implant placement and gum/bone health; excellent for esthetic cases and grafting.
- Prosthodontists or restorative dental specialists: important when the final crown, bridge, or implant-supported denture is complex — they design the restoration.
- High-volume implant centers / All-on-4 specialists (if you need full-arch replacement): some practices do same-day teeth; ask about long-term outcomes and who does the final restoration.
- Full-service practices that do both surgery and restoration in-house: convenient coordination and fewer handoffs.

What I’ll prioritize when picking specific clinics for you
- Board certification and specialist credentials (AAOMS for surgeons, AAP board-certified periodontists, prosthodontist credentials)
- Experience with the procedure you need (single implant vs full-arch)
- Availability of CBCT 3D imaging (important for planning)
- On-site sedation/IV sedation if needed
- Positive before/after photos and patient reviews
- Transparent pricing, warranty/guarantee on restorations, and financing options

Questions to ask when you call (quick script)
- “Do you place dental implants? How many implant cases do you do per year?”
- “Are you a board-certified oral surgeon / periodontist / prosthodontist?”
- “Do you do the surgical placement and the restorative crown/denture here, or will I need a separate restorative dentist?”
- “Do you use CBCT 3D imaging and digital planning?”
- “What implant brands do you use and do you offer warranties?”
- “Estimated timeline and typical total cost (including grafting and final restoration)?”
- “Do you accept my insurance and do you offer financing?”
- “Do you provide IV sedation or nitrous oxide?”

If you tell me your zip code/neighborhood and the type of implant you need, I’ll compile a short list (5–8) of specific practices in Atlanta with brief reasons to call each, plus phone/website links and a recommended first choice based on your priorities.
